rules.description: Deserializing user-controlled data may allow attackers to execute arbitrary code.

rules.cwe_name: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
rules.description: A regular expression that requires exponential time to match certain inputs can be a performance bottleneck, and may be vulnerable to denial-of-service attacks.

rules.cwe_name: Observable Timing Discrepancy
rules.description: Use of a non-constant-time verification routine to check the value of an HTTP header, possibly allowing a timing attack to infer the header's expected value.

rules.cwe_name: Sensitive Cookie with Improper SameSite Attribute
rules.description: Cookies with `SameSite` set to `None` can allow for Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) attacks.

rules.cwe_name: Function Call with Incorrectly Specified Arguments
rules.description: Using a named argument whose name does not correspond to a parameter of the called function or method, will result in a TypeError at runtime.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers ('HTTP Request/Response Splitting')
rules.description: Writing user input directly to an HTTP header makes code vulnerable to attack by header splitting.
